newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania grants 1,400 billion lei to private farms.
newsitem.headline: Romania grants 1,400 billion lei to private farms.

text.p: Romania's Agriculture Ministry will grant 1,400 billion lei to private farmers to help them with the cost of seasonal works, a senior ministry official said on Wednesday.
"We will give private farmers coupons worth 140,000 lei each. They will get one coupon for each hectare they own," Adorian Kovacs, State Secretary at the Agriculture Ministry, told Reuters.

"Farmers can use the coupons to cover part of the costs for seeds, fertilisers, fuel, harvesting or any other farm work," Kovacs said, adding the coupons would be distributed to farmers by early July.
He made the remarks after a conference marking the start of harvesting.

Reports in the local media say costs related to seasonal works on a hectare of grains amount to some 800,000 lei. Romania has around 14 million hectares of agricultural land, including orchards, vinyards and pastures.
The move is part of the government's programme to help the cash-strapped private farming sector, Kovacs said.
"I want to make it clear that these non-reimbursable funds come from the ministry's reserves so the project will have no inflationary effects," he said.

Under 1990 land reform farmers were granted title deeds for land nationalised in the 1950s by the Communists. But land was returned with an upper limit of 10 hectares per person regardless of how much was owned before nationalisation. Parliament is expected to discuss next month a proposal by the centrist coalition to return to farmers all the lands they owned before the 1950s.

But many Romanian farmers cannot cope with the high interest rates, of up to 90 percent, asked by commercial banks on credits. Kovacs said banks should adopt a more flexible stand when giving credits to the farming sector, which last year contributed more than 20 percent to the country's GDP.

"Banks should not turn a blind eye to problems in the farming sector. They should give credits with affordable interest rates and at the right time," he said. --Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
